_what_this_is: Deliberate defects injected into REAL source on a throwaway copy. Each must make
the gate go red. One that escapes is a class of bug that can currently merge with
THIS FILE IS PROTECTED. A builder that can edit its own defect set can pass it.
_how_to_write_one: id      a name that says what broke, not which line changed
file    path relative to the repo root
find    an exact snippet from that file. Keep it SHORT and distinctive -- a long
anchor breaks the moment anyone reformats, and a broken anchor is
reported as NOT_INJECTED rather than silently passing
replace what to put there instead
why     what it would mean if this escaped. You write this before you know
whether it does, and it is the sentence you will read when it escapes
_this_repo: Five defects, one per static/unit rung that exists today: parse, i18n, two type
ratchets, and the auth-ordering ratchet. The e2e and holdout rungs cannot be
faulted until a journey agent is installed (harness.config.json agent.cmd) and the
web console runs on :5178; run.py refuses to score against a red gate, so adding
defects aimed at rungs that cannot run would only manufacture a fake number.
Every anchor below is a single line, so a reformat reports NOT_INJECTED instead of
_copy: What to copy into each throwaway build. Must cover every input the gate's commands read, plus node_modules, which run.py links in rather than copies.

defects.why: Unbalanced parenthesis: the whole WMS manager patrol script fails to parse, so every patrol run crashes before it queries anything.
A shop-floor label renders as an empty string on the Vietnamese console; a grep for the key finds a definition, so only a per-locale check catches it.

defects.replace:
const __MUTANT: number = "x";
export const locales: Locale[] = ["zh-CN", "vi-VN", "en-US"];
defects.why: A type error that a bundler happily strips: the build still runs, the console shows garbage where the number should be.
The type ratchet exists precisely so services/api can drift one error at a time instead of all at once; an escape means new type rot is invisible.
